pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a good way to give feedback to a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at mistakes
   B. Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   C. Say nothing
   D. Say they are bad

2. What is a group of lines in a poem called? (1 mark)
   A. A sentence
   B. A chapter
   C. A paragraph
   D. A stanza

3. Which way of reading a sad part is best? (1 mark)
   A. Slowly and softly
   B. Without pausing
   C. Fast and loud
   D. Laughing

4. What should a dialogue about leisure show? (1 mark)
   A. Bad habits
   B. Unkindness
   C. Rudeness
   D. Good values such as responsibility

5. In the passage: Ugali is made from maize flour, what is ugali made from? (1 mark)
   A. rice
   B. wheat only
   C. maize flour
   D. millet

6. Does every poem have to rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. No
   B. Only long poems
   C. Yes, always
   D. Only short poems

7. Which is a mistake in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Using a full stop
   B. Using a question
   C. Using a name
   D. Forgetting the colon after the name

8. What is the meaning of reciting a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Copying it
   B. Erasing it
   C. Writing it
   D. Saying it aloud, usually from memory

9. What is the difference between a proverb and a story? (1 mark)
   A. They are the same
   B. A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   C. A proverb has many characters
   D. A story is shorter

10. A sentence should end with a (1 mark)
   A. full stop
   B. drawing
   C. capital letter
   D. comma

11. What is the message of a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The number of lines
   B. The main idea the poet wants to share
   C. The date
   D. The printer

12. What does the Kiswahili proverb Haba na haba hujaza kibaba teach? (1 mark)
   A. Small amounts added together become a lot
   B. Big things are useless
   C. Only large amounts count
   D. Never save

13. What is a good way to learn interjections in your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. Guess meanings
   B. Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   C. Ignore them
   D. Invent them

14. What is an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. A word that names a person
   B. A word that shows action
   C. A word that describes a noun
   D. A joining word

15. What is a vocabulary bank? (1 mark)
   A. A place for money
   B. A list of useful words on a theme
   C. A kind of poem
   D. A book cover

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write a four-sentence paragraph on washing hands. Use first, next, then and finally. (4 marks)

17. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about why we should write neatly. Check your capital letters and full stops. (5 marks)

18. Divide into subject and predicate: My brother saves coins. (2 marks)

19. Correct this paragraph: it was a cold morning in nyeri the children wore sweaters scarves and socks (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   Kind and useful feedback helps people improve.

2. D — A stanza
   A stanza is a group of lines.

3. A — Slowly and softly
   A slow, soft voice matches sadness.

4. D — Good values such as responsibility
   Dialogues can teach values.

5. C — maize flour
   The passage states that ugali is made from maize flour.

6. A — No
   Some poems do not rhyme.

7. D — Forgetting the colon after the name
   The colon is needed after the name.

8. D — Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   To recite is to say aloud.

9. B — A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   Proverbs are very short.

10. A — full stop
   A statement ends with a full stop.

11. B — The main idea the poet wants to share
   The message is the main idea.

12. A — Small amounts added together become a lot
   The proverb means little by little fills the measure.

13. B — Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   Learning from speakers is reliable.

14. C — A word that describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

15. B — A list of useful words on a theme
   A word bank stores words to learn.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, wet your hands. Next, rub soap on them. Then rinse them. Finally, dry them with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in order and sequence word.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three neat, complete sentences, for example Neat writing helps others to read my work. It shows respect for the reader. I feel proud when my book is tidy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence, one mark for capital letters and one for full stops.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: Subject: My brother. Predicate: saves coins.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: It was a cold morning in Nyeri. The children wore sweaters, scarves and socks.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four corrections: capitals at the start, Nyeri, the full stops and the commas.
